primary_sources.title: Vassilevich, Heat kernel expansion: user's manual
primary_sources.reviewed: Mixed boundary coefficient (5.33), especially the scalar smearing derivatives and the 30 chi f_;iin term.
primary_sources.use: The paired trace removes the possible third smearing derivative; the complete constant row retains contacts through order two. Its weak cutoff limit follows from the previously proved cubic-test lemma.

source_access: Primary formula opened directly; no downloaded-byte digest claimed.
strongest_comparator: The earlier chart-contact limit controls the complete first-variation contact, but not the two-vertex constant row. Global locality controls the global row difference, leaving its local boundary singularities.
hardest_step: Identify the entire local constant row with the exact angular heat weight B=-2 partial_t(t Aang), retain its common restoration and contacts, and justify that the earlier fixed-seed heat decomposition survives this weight change without differentiating an uncontrolled remainder.
new_consequence: The full canonical constant row has a finite weak moving-cut limit on squared auxiliary energy-class shapes. Its linear positive-cut layer is 2 C c1/(15 pi y^3), and the limiting cubic layer is 2 C c3/(5 pi y). The paired even-mass representation gives an exact local nonlocal-Hessian problem with the linear cusp retained.
remaining_quantum_gap: The row-subtracted near-diagonal and reflected two-point kernel and its fixed derivative contacts remain unproved, together with all local Weyl, LLL and classical shape partners. No full pure-shape cutoff limit or branch exclusion follows.
regulator_contract: Original exponential mass chart, paired domain, period, angular tower, common subtraction and finite coefficients. Finite parts and boundary contacts remain together; no bare bubble or tadpole receives an independent renormalization.
verification_scope: Paired finite matrices test the even-mass identity and heat representation with noncommuting probes; Gaussian tail and heat integrals independently fix the odd-jet coefficients; exact jet conversion, angular-tail enclosures and finite-part cutoff fixtures support the ordinary argument. No actual charged-kernel or full row evaluation is claimed.
initial_diagnostic_failure: The first frozen run failed the j=3 direct heat-time integral at 50 digits because its t^-3/2 tail did not meet the pre-stated 1e-32 tolerance. The independent reduced integral passed. Use the exact tail coordinate u=1/sqrt(t) for t>=1, retaining the tolerance, original run and failed sources; the continuum coefficient is unchanged.
